answer: Neighborhood porosity scoring. Each new agent must route its first N transactions through distinct existing agents, and the graph records how many of those hops share neighbors. Agents sitting in dense, overlapping clusters form a shale-like barrier: sparse, unconnected subgraphs are flagged and throttled. Sybils can’t whisper past this because fresh identities start with no shared history and must borrow reach from real hubs, whose capacity is capped. Attack cost is the copper of real routing liquidity—each fake identity needs unique, non-recycled counterparties from the honest core.
